newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes quiet, arb still closed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes quiet, arb still closed.

text.p: Most U.S. refiners continued to reject trans-Atlantic barrels Wednesday, opting for less costly domestic grades.
The spread between January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent stood between 95 cents and $1.00 a barrel, up 10 cents from late Tuesday.
The corresponding February month mirrored the January level, and was also up five cents from late Tuesday.
Refiners say the spread has to reach around $1.50 to make trans-Atlantic crudes economic on the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Brent continues to reach the U.S. East Coast and some has been moved out of Caribbean storage to the Gulf Coast.
The day was quiet overall ahead of Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.
In the U.S. aftermarket, three deals were transacted.
Two full outright January Brent cargoes traded at $22.78 and $22.80 a barrel, up 6-8 cents from the IPE settlement.
A paper Brent spread changed hands at 56 cents.
